purpose: Downstream open-loop exploratory model-space orientation from frozen Phase25 proxies; no predicted biological yaw.

yaw_mapping.sign_evidence: Erginkaya2025 Fig7: left perturbation produces rightward drift; right perturbation produces leftward drift. Remaining-side dominance is a qualitative inference, not an isolated graded motor law.
yaw_mapping.scale_rationale: Unit model-space coordinate normalization; selected without inspecting yaw output or source peak; no physiological magnitude.

orientation_model.normalization_rationale: One unit held yaw-drive over the entire frozen 50ms horizon contributes one orientation_eq; no biological temporal claim.

analytical_bounds.proof: Bounded signed descriptors, neutral initial states and exact exponential convex updates keep HS and DNp15 within [-1,1]. Hence |R-L|<=2, |drive|<=2, and sum(dt/H)=1 implies |orientation-initial|<=2 for the finite horizon.
analytical_bounds.neutral_behavior: Equal bilateral target states give zero drive and unchanged neutral orientation.

assumptions.name: Proxy activity -> odd linear orientation drive and bilateral symmetry
Unit proxy scale and global horizon-normalized integration
Source time grid and left-boundary/final-boundary convention

acceptance: Accept zero, small, opposite-signed or unexpected internally valid outcomes. No retuning after first frozen execution.
claim_limits: Exploratory DNp15-linked model-space orientation, not a measured DNp15 motor command
Not biological yaw, calibrated turn rate, torque or biomechanics
Not navigation, full optomotor behavior or closed-loop course stabilization
Negative proxy/reversal symmetry is a model extension, not measured negative activity
